progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: Fresh Year 12 students know plants contain cells. Earlier B1/B2 introduced reproduction and sperm/egg joining; this lesson supplies the meanings and physical flower locations it needs. No meiosis or chromosome knowledge.
progression.startsWith: Pollen arrives on a flower, but the egg lies inside an ovule.
progression.stopsAfter: Explain the embryo-forming pollen-tube route and why a stopped tube can leave pollination complete without fertilising this egg. Ovule becomes seed containing an embryo; complete double fertilisation and germination physiology deferred.
progression.nextLesson: bio-m5-b02b delivery part 2: How does a strawberry runner make a new plant?

teaching.task: Explain why pollen arrival needs a pollen-tube route before an embryo forms inside a seed.
teaching.causalExplanation: Pollen arrives at stigma while egg is elsewhere inside ovule. Compatible pollen grows a tube that carries sperm to the egg. Joining starts embryo development; surrounding ovule develops into seed. Stopping that route before the only ovule prevents this egg from being fertilised.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Introduce each term with an object and action in the current picture. Retain only the current causal sentence. Explain before classifying or offering a memory contrast.
teaching.openingDecision: Ask whether receiving pollen already makes a new plant. Address that precise confusion through the route and stopped-tube case; no generic mistake/fix scene.
teaching.understandingCheck: Compatible pollen reaches stigma, tube stops before the only ovule and no other tube reaches it. Students decide pollination, egg fertilisation and whether this embryo-forming route can continue. All conditions and demands remain during a separate quiet hold.
teaching.curriculumScope: Focused candidate contribution to B-plants in canonical bio-m5-b02b. Flower and runner are separate delivery parts. Source presence and visual fit do not establish reviewed action coverage.
